source_text.ISS-0348: mix letflow.check (full serial mix test) exits 1 with 4 failures in test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs, all {updated, skipped} count-mismatch assertions on Backfill.run/1's tally. Does not manifest under scripts/test_parallel.sh's partitioned execution. Suspected DB-state pollution: BackfillTest is async:false/Sandbox :auto so it sees tenant rows other tests left committed. See docs/issues/ISS-0348.yaml for full description and acceptance_criteria.

task.description: ISSUE-FIXER: Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0348. Do NOT implement a fix.
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5: check docs/issues/ for resolved entries with matching DB-pollution/test-isolation symptoms in tenant_provisioning tests -- if a recurrence, flag severity accordingly

Step 1: reproduce directly -- run `mix test` in FULL SERIAL mode (not scripts/test_parallel.sh) at least twice and quote real output showing the 4 BackfillTest failures (or confirm/refute reproduction -- flakes can be nondeterministic)

Identify the specific other test(s) that commit tenant/tenant_schema rows visible to BackfillTest's scan under serial ordering -- grep for tests that insert into tenants/tenant_schemas without full cleanup, or that use Sandbox :auto without a transaction rollback
Trace Backfill.run/1's tenant-scan query to understand exactly what rows it would pick up that a properly-isolated test wouldn't leave behind
Do NOT implement the fix -- write result.summary with root cause (not symptom), affected files, what a fix needs to change; next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design

registry_lookup.searched: grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for Sandbox/test-isolation/tenant_schemas/DB-pollution symptoms; read every hit's title/description
registry_lookup.finding: No prior RESOLVED entry with this exact symptom (BackfillTest count-mismatch). But ISS-0113 (status: open, MINOR, filed by ISSUE-FIXER in WF03-ISS0109-20260821) already diagnosed the exact underlying mechanism this issue's failures depend on: `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` is a GLOBAL, repo-wide setting (not per-test), and TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (and ~5 other async:false modules: tenant_provisioning_test.exs, tenant_onboarding_test.exs, routers/onboarding_test.exs, routers/tenants_test.exs, event_store/registry_test.exs) switch it to :auto and never restore :manual. ISS-0113 also recorded a REVERTED fix attempt: a blanket restore-to-:manual inside the shared TenantFixture helper broke 12 other tests across 3 distinct mechanisms (double-checkout collisions, concurrent-lock tests needing real :auto access, and tests provisioning a second schema mid-test needing :auto for Ecto.Migrator). This is not a fresh recurrence of a resolved bug -- it is ISS-0348 being the first *observed failure* attributed to the previously-theoretical ISS-0113 gap ('no failure has been attributed to it' -- ISS-0113's own text). Severity stays MAJOR as filed (CI-blocking), but CODE-DESIGNER must read ISS-0113's investigation_note in full before proposing a fix: a naive global :auto->:manual restore is a known-bad shape here.

reproduction.verdict: NOT reproduced in either of 2 full-serial runs today. This is consistent with the root-cause theory below rather than refuting it: the pollution depends on which OTHER async:false module(s) happen to run, and in what order, before backfill_test.exs under ExUnit's per-invocation random seed -- it is not a static, always-on defect. RELEASE-VALIDATOR's original WF03-ISS0347 run did observe it (4/4 BackfillTest failures, quoted verbatim in docs/issues/ISS-0348.yaml), so the failure mode is real, just seed/order-dependent and did not land on either seed drawn during this diagnosis session.

result.summary:
ROOT CAUSE (not symptom): Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill.run/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:20) does `Repo.all(Registration)` -- an UNSCOPED, whole-table scan of every tenant Registration row in the database, then calls Registry.register_type/2 for each one and tallies {updated, skipped}. It has no filter to the tenant(s) a given test actually created. This design is safe ONLY if the DB contains exactly the rows the running test itself provisioned at the moment Backfill.run/1 executes -- i.e. only if Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox is providing real per-test isolation for every other test that has run earlier in the same `mix test` invocation.

That isolation guarantee is exactly what ISS-0113 already found to be broken: Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode/2 is a REPO-WIDE global, not a per-test setting. TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:169, used by backfill_test.exs itself) and at least 5 other async:false test modules (test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs, tenant_onboarding_test.exs, routers/onboarding_test.exs, routers/tenants_test.exs, event_store/registry_test.exs) call `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` to get a real, unsandboxed connection (required because Ecto.Migrator/replay_migrations cannot run inside a wrapping sandbox transaction) and deliberately never restore :manual afterward (documented, accepted debt -- ISS-0113, and TenantFixture's own moduledoc INV-F-6 cites it by name as out of scope). Once :auto is set, it stays set for every subsequent test in the same BEAM/mix-test process, regardless of that later test's own `async:`/DataCase setup expectations, until some other test happens to flip it back.

All of the modules above DO register their own on_exit/1 cleanup that deletes their own Registration/Tenant/schema rows (verified by reading test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's teardown/2 and the on_exit blocks in tenant_onboarding_test.exs, routers/onboarding_test.exs, routers/tenants_test.exs, event_store/registry_test.exs), so under NORMAL completion they self-clean and leave nothing for BackfillTest to see. The failure window is narrower and order/timing-dependent: (a) any test whose on_exit callback does not run to completion (a hard process crash rather than an assertion failure, or an exception inside the on_exit callback itself before its DELETE statements execute) leaves its Registration/Tenant rows permanently committed (no wrapping transaction to roll them back once mode is :auto); or (b) any OTHER, unrelated async:false test elsewhere in the suite that inserts a Registration/Tenant/tenant_schemas row via plain Ecto.Repo calls without itself calling Sandbox.mode(:auto) or registering matching cleanup, believing (correctly, if mode were still :manual/{:shared,pid} as Letflow.DataCase's setup normally arranges) that DataCase's checkout+shared-transaction will roll its writes back -- but if that test executes AFTER some earlier module already flipped global mode to :auto and before anything flips it back, its writes are real, permanent commits instead. Because ExUnit's module execution order is seed-randomized (test/test_helper.exs:9 -- `ExUnit.start(exclude: [:keycloak])`, no fixed --seed), which of these two windows fires, and whether it fires at all, varies run to run -- exactly matching the issue's own observation that it appears under `mix letflow.check`'s full-serial invocation but not scripts/test_parallel.sh (separate BEAM/partition processes never share the leaked global Sandbox mode) and did not reproduce in either of this diagnosis session's 2 runs.

I was not able to pin the diagnosis to one single named leaking test in this session (issue did not reproduce to observe it directly), but I've fully traced the CLASS of culprit and the exact mechanism: any Repo write to `tenants`/`tenant_schemas`/`event_type_registry` (Registration-adjacent tables) that (a) executes while Sandbox mode is globally :auto due to an earlier test's leak per ISS-0113, and (b) is not followed by matching on_exit cleanup, leaves rows Backfill.run/1's unscoped `Repo.all(Registration)` will pick up in a later, unrelated test. A next diagnostic step for whoever designs the fix (CODE-DESIGNER, or an ISSUE-FIXER rerun with a captured failing --seed) would be to run with a fixed `--seed` from a run that DOES fail and bisect module order, or add temporary instrumentation logging Registration row count immediately before backfill_test.exs's first test.

AFFECTED FILES:
  - lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex (Backfill.run/1, line 20: `Repo.all(Registration)` -- the unscoped scan that makes BackfillTest sensitive to ANY stray Registration row anywhere in the DB)
  - test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs (the 4 assertions asserting exact {updated, skipped} counts against a scan whose input set the test does not fully control)
  - test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (provisioned_tenant!/1, the :auto-mode source used by backfill_test.exs itself and 5+ other modules)
  - docs/issues/ISS-0113.yaml (prior, still-open diagnosis of the underlying Sandbox-mode-leak mechanism; contains a documented REVERTED fix attempt and its 3 failure mechanisms -- required reading before designing a new fix)

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE (for CODE-DESIGNER, not implemented here):
  1. Either (a) scope Backfill.run/1's query to a caller-supplied tenant_id list / exclude a way to run against 'only tenants this call cares about' in production callers while giving BackfillTest a way to assert against a KNOWN, bounded set of registrations (e.g. by filtering to the tenant_ids the test itself created, if Backfill.run/1's contract can add an optional scope without changing its production (whole-fleet sweep) semantics) -- this fixes the SYMPTOM (test assertions) without touching the Sandbox-leak root cause; or (b) actually close the ISS-0113 gap so no stray committed rows exist when BackfillTest runs -- ISS-0113's own investigation_note already shows a blanket fix is unsafe (12 tests break across 3 distinct mechanisms: double-checkout collisions, concurrent-lock tests requiring real :auto access, and tests provisioning a second schema mid-test needing Ecto.Migrator's :auto requirement) and recommends a per-caller opt-in (e.g. `opts[:restore_sandbox]` on provisioned_tenant!/1, defaulting to false/unchanged) verified individually against each of those 3 failure mechanisms for each of the ~6 call sites -- this is the more invasive but structurally correct option.
  2. Whichever direction is chosen, the fix must not weaken BackfillTest's actual regression coverage for ISS-0332/ISS-0343 (issue's own 2nd acceptance criterion) -- e.g. scoping the query must still exercise the real Registry.register_type/2 code path Backfill.run/1 uses in production, not stub it out.
  3. mix letflow.check must be run and pass with exit 0 as final verification (issue's 3rd acceptance criterion), and scripts/test_parallel.sh must stay green (4th) -- both need re-verification after the fix, not assumed from this diagnosis.
